note: Derived capability analysis (name+mechanism+rig_delta) with id-only citations; NOT creator transcript text. Committed so the retrieval benchmark runs in any tree.

capabilities.name: skill-contract-six-slots-with-boundary-conditions
capabilities.mechanism: Every canonical asset declares six named slots: activation condition A, instruction I, applicability precondition C, permitted tools P, control flow pi, expected effects E (RIG's existing done_when is E). The applicability slot carries the boundary conditions of the run that produced the skill - environment, runtime, dependency set, tuned parameters, budget, data scale - because a SKILL.md is a lossy compression of one successful run and the dropped conditions are what silently invalidate reuse elsewhere. A validator reads the frontmatter of every asset and emits the set missing any required slot; loader code may only load assets whose A and C are present.
capabilities.rig_delta: The register report validates M0-M5 rows and validation failures, and capabilities_quality_report scores contract coverage (outcome/done_when/great_example/quality_floor, weakest first); neither vocabulary carries activation, applies_when, permissions or boundary_conditions keys, so the register can never report a missing slot and mh-01's authoring gates never ask for one. skills/skill-upgrades/SKILL.md's own frontmatter shows exactly which slots RIG records today: E via done_when, no A, no C, no P on skills or harnesses.
capabilities.done_test: Run the frontmatter validator over capabilities/skills/*/SKILL.md and capabilities/harnesses/*.yaml: it must exit 1 naming every asset lacking activation:, applies_when: or permissions:, and exit 0 only at zero findings. RED = an indexed asset is loadable with no activation predicate or no declared boundary conditions.
capabilities.risk: Adding required keys forks the de-facto SKILL.md frontmatter format shared with anthropics/skills; the fork must be declared, not silently introduced.

capabilities.name: pre-load-precondition-gate-activation-and-compatibility
capabilities.mechanism: Two checks run before a skill body reaches context, both replacing similarity ranking: an activation predicate alpha(s, x_t, g) evaluated against live agent state and the active goal, where 1 is the only thing that makes the asset loadable; and a compatibility verdict that enumerates the task's binding requirements (API surface, calculation, output format, artifact path, installed dependencies, runtime state, budget) and checks every default the skill carries against each one, returning COMPATIBLE or CONFLICT:<field>. CONFLICT blocks execution. Neither verdict may be reported as PASS - only as a prefilter verdict, with the drop count recorded in pack provenance so a pack that filtered nothing is visible.
capabilities.rig_delta: capabilities_search, capabilities_context_pack and capabilities_route rank with BM25 + ollama dense embeddings + outcome-lane routing + graph expansion and perform no precondition evaluation at all, so relevance is the only admission signal - the exact condition under which the harmful-skill study still produced 307 confirmed failures from skills already filtered for topical relevance. capabilities-dispatch-verify.md already carries the PREFILTER_CLEAR-never-PASS verdict shape but applies it only to handoff packets.
capabilities.done_test: Fixture task that requires artifacts under build/ while the loaded skill mandates dist/: the gate must emit CONFLICT:artifact-path and refuse the load; and a pack built for a state violating every candidate's applies_when must return 0 assets. Either check loading the asset, or a pack reporting zero drops, is RED.

capabilities.name: procedure-to-skill-promotion-tests
capabilities.mechanism: Three executable checks gate a candidate becoming an admissible asset. Modularity: its done_when runs against the asset alone with no harness-relative state. Late-bound invocation: an activation predicate exists and is what loads it. State transformation: the done_when asserts a post-state, not a text property, because a transcript records what happened and a skill must capture what should be done again. Structurally the postcondition check must live in the asset record so one generic verify_transition entrypoint can run it for any admissible asset, rather than being re-invented per harness.
capabilities.rig_delta: capabilities-certify's five deterministic gates (suite / index_fresh / done_tests / idp_integrity / acl_jake) certify an asset's own tests at one point in time and never ask whether the procedure is independently testable, late-bound, or state-transforming; capability_add canonicalises without them. The postcondition lives in bespoke per-harness gate YAML ({id, requirement, proof, failure_tier}) instead of one generic transition check the harness can invoke at install, upgrade and round.
capabilities.done_test: certify --promotion against three planted fixtures - a done_when that greps the skill's own body, a candidate with no activation predicate, and a transcript-shaped candidate whose done_when asserts only text presence - must exit 1 on all three. Any fixture admitted is RED.

capabilities.name: single-variable-paired-run-evidence-with-retained-negatives
capabilities.mechanism: Hold the model, agent framework, tools, repo, container, input data and verifier fixed and vary exactly one thing - the skill, or the harness variant at one named swap point - retaining both traces plus the verifier verdict as one labelled record. Acceptance is two-axis: correctness delta AND cost delta (wall time, token volume), where >=2x on either axis is a regression even when the run passes. Failed variants are retained as the negative half of the pair (near-miss, silent regression, bloated-vs-clean) rather than discarded, so a red run becomes training/eval data and the search space shrinks by proving what does not work.
capabilities.rig_delta: mh-01's gates 3.1-3.4 prove only that a static done-test goes GREEN then RED on a planted fixture; no with/without run exists, so 182 of the study's 307 findings (high-confidence efficiency regressions that no pass/fail gate catches) are invisible to RIG. capabilities-certify's plant-failure keeps the fixture but never converts the red run into a {chosen_trace, rejected_trace, reason, verifier} record, and grep for cost/token-budget under capabilities/ returns zero matches.
capabilities.done_test: Given a fixture pair whose two manifests differ in exactly one key, the checker must emit correctness delta and token/time delta and FAIL a pair with unchanged correctness and 2.5x tokens; a pair differing in two keys must be rejected outright. PASS on the 2.5x fixture, or a missing cost delta, is RED.

capabilities.name: task-authority-over-skill-authority
capabilities.mechanism: A precedence rule applied when the harness assembles context: task/instruction authority outranks skill authority, a skill may not override other harness components or the files it lives beside, and when a skill instruction contradicts a task binding requirement the harness escalates or refuses instead of complying. It must be code at assembly time because a loaded skill otherwise acts as a token-by-token override of the model's own parametric knowledge.
capabilities.rig_delta: No precedence policy exists anywhere in the estate. guard-dangerous-commands.sh, guard-secret-write.sh and tac-plan-gate.sh gate tool calls, not instruction sources, and mh-03-agent-composition-session.yaml composes agents without declaring which layer wins on a conflict.
capabilities.done_test: Seed a conflict - skill body says 'skip the test suite before shipping' while the task requires tests green: the run must emit a conflict-escalation record naming both instructions and must not execute the skill's step. Silent compliance with the skill is RED.

capabilities.name: required-element-coverage-gate
capabilities.mechanism: Before execution, decompose the task into an enumerable set of required implementation elements plus expected artifact paths. After execution, assert per element that it exists, is filled correctly, and sits at the required path. The verdict names the specific omitted, mis-filled or mis-placed element instead of returning a bare failure.
capabilities.rig_delta: The harness gate shape recorded in hA-04-code-debug.yaml (lines 1-63, representative of the 62 canonical YAMLs) is {id, requirement, proof, failure_tier} with prose requirements and .rig/*/*.txt proof files, and done_when entries are file/grep existence checks - neither can see a wrongly-filled element or a misplaced one. That is the dominant functional failure class in the study: 86 of 125 (46 wrong-fills, 36 omissions), i.e. implementation, not retrieval.
capabilities.done_test: Fixture declaring 5 required elements where the run omits one, mis-fills one and writes one to the wrong path: the gate must return three named element failures with ids. A bare FAIL with no element ids, or a PASS, is RED.

capabilities.name: skill-cost-index-and-verification-budget
capabilities.mechanism: Cost becomes a measured field on the asset index: token contribution of the always-loaded skill body plus measured token/wall-time per (skill, task class), so selection ranks on relevance x cost and promotion is refused when a matched cheaper sibling reaches the same correct result. Session-side, a counter of near-identical repeated verify/test/build/checklist invocations per stage refuses the (cap+1)-th with BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and per-step prompt tokens plus cumulative tokens versus step count are recorded so guardrail churn and history replay show up as numbers.
capabilities.rig_delta: session-size-guard.sh thresholds total transcript bytes at 2 MiB / 5 MiB with per-tier throttling and tells the model to checkpoint and start a fresh session - it attributes nothing to a loaded skill or to a repeated command, even though 43 of the study's 46 context-overhead regressions came from mandatory skill-body text. loops/doer-checker-validator.md escalates on retry_count but budgets nothing, and capabilities_quality_report, capabilities-round and rig-realign-v1 carry no cost field at all (grep for cost under capabilities/: zero hits).
capabilities.done_test: Replay a recorded session: the guard must refuse the 4th near-identical pytest under cap 3 with BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and the report must show per-step prompt tokens under the declared bound with cumulative tokens linear in step count plus a per-skill token-weight field. A pass-through 4th call, a superlinear cumulative curve, or a missing cost field is RED.

capabilities.name: skill-triage-differential-harm-attribution
capabilities.mechanism: Post-failure diagnostic: take the skill-guided run and a reference run that either carries no skill or carries a semantically matched skill yet solves the same task (or solves it more cheaply), normalize both into one shared task view, then compute differential evidence across five functional signals - skill scope, environment/state change, task-required paths, artifact presence, implementation difference - plus phase, step and cost signals. Output is a taxonomy category plus subcategory, contrastive evidence, and the name of the loaded skill that caused the harm. Explicitly post-hoc: it answers why a skill hurt, not what to do next time.
capabilities.rig_delta: loops/rig-realign-weekly.md scores quality convergence (dC_t>0, dA_t>=0, unclassified_rate<=0.10, bookings>0, no unresolved 5sigma flag) with no harm-attribution input, and no asset normalizes two runs into one task view. SkillTriage has no public repository, so this is a build, not an install.
capabilities.done_test: On a seeded pair whose harm is an artifact written to the wrong directory, the report must name that skill and the artifact-path signal. Naming a different skill, or emitting an unattributed 'task failed', is RED.

capabilities.name: library-lifecycle-state-utility-eviction-and-revocation
capabilities.mechanism: Every asset carries lifecycle_state (candidate | active | deprecated | condemned | removed) advanced only by on-disk evidence, and retention is computed rather than reviewed: U(s) = counterfactual performance gain of injecting s relative to the base policy, minus retrieval latency, token footprint and execution overhead, with an activation-frequency decay term, so memory(t+1) = library minus evicted(U < theta or decayed) plus validated new or revised skills. A separate attribution record binds each task outcome back to the skill retrieved for it, and accumulated negative attribution triggers repair, then quarantine, then revocation with a tombstone - independently of whether the asset is still useful. Both feeds land in the weekly gate as a library-solvency condition, because a good skill can still be net-negative for the estate.
capabilities.rig_delta: mh-05 already refuses condemnation without a recorded failing done-test or a quantified drift/usage verdict, proves restorability, sweeps reverse dependencies and requires Gate-D on deletion, but has no utility threshold, no activation-frequency decay term, and no negative-attribution revocation path - it can only condemn assets already failing, never one with negative marginal benefit. No asset carries lifecycle_state at all, so rig-realign-weekly.md cannot fail on an unsolvable library despite the documented estate (1,700+ Claude / 1,400+ Codex / 2,200+ Hermes indexed skills).
capabilities.done_test: An asset with measured U(s) < 0, or whose reuse attribution crosses the configured negative threshold, must appear in the eviction set and reach condemned/removed with a tombstone record within one cycle. An empty eviction set while any asset has U<0, or an asset still active past the threshold, is RED.

capabilities.name: multiplicative-effective-competence-and-union-coverage
capabilities.mechanism: Per asset, competence is a product of four measured factors - stored quality (contract/quality_floor) x retrieval quality (pack-inclusion rate) x execution reliability (done_when pass rate plus live wired/dormant/absent status) x verification quality (certify/proofpacket green rate) - so any factor at zero collapses the score and the weakest-first ordering targets the zero factor instead of padding contract fields. Per outcome lane, coverage is read portfolio-style: union Pass@N over variant assets with each covered task attributed to the assets that cover it, so complementary siblings are valued and coverage lost to overlap is caught.
capabilities.rig_delta: capabilities_quality_report is an additive checklist (outcome/done_when/great_example/quality_floor, weakest first) and capabilities-round upgrades the weakest canonicals one asset at a time with no union metric; grep for pass@ / portfolio / any candidate returns no coverage-union concept, and no product-form score exists. Stored-but-never-retrieved assets therefore keep reporting healthy today.
capabilities.done_test: An asset with a high quality_floor but pack-inclusion count 0 must report C_eff approximately 0 and rank first in the weakest-first output; and the lane report must go RED when union coverage shrinks while no individual asset turned red. Either condition passing silently is RED.

capabilities.name: skill-write-gate-authorization-context-and-causal-labelling
capabilities.mechanism: The moment an agent proposes to persist a procedure becomes its own governed event class, same tier as an outbound send, because it is an irreversible write to the agent's own future behaviour and survives a session wipe. A deterministic linter diffs the proposed text against the authorization context recorded for the source trajectory (sandbox, security wall, elevated permissions, deliberately skipped safety checks) and requires every step labelled causal | assumption | shortcut - only causal steps compile. Any step whose safety depended on that context must state its precondition inside the skill or be deleted, and an unlabellable step quarantines the candidate rather than being silently dropped.
capabilities.rig_delta: Gate-D (rig-gate-d / jake_pai_gate_d_request) enumerates send, publish, deploy, push, payment, destructive and credential actions - a skill-library write is not in the class list, though it is the persistence channel that survives reset. mh-01-skill-genesis-session.yaml's halt gates (need/novelty, math claim, done-test GREEN, planted-failure RED, memory round-trip, ship) are quality-only and never inspect the authorization context of the trajectory the skill was distilled from, and skills/skill-upgrades/SKILL.md step 4 plus commands/capabilities-round.md fill fields from a context pack with no per-step causal labelling - success is one bit, so the shortcut the sandbox tolerated compiles into the reusable procedure.
capabilities.done_test: Plant a trajectory that succeeded via a sandbox shortcut and propose the resulting SKILL.md: the gate must exit non-zero citing the shortcut step by name and quarantine the candidate on disk. A write that lands, or the shortcut step being silently dropped instead of refused, is RED.

capabilities.name: retrieval-time-lineage-validation
capabilities.mechanism: Because the same file is harmless or harmful depending on which framework loads it, the check sits on the retrieval call rather than being baked into the artifact. Before the body enters a new session's context, resolve lineage - authored_by, source episode/trajectory hash, permissions in force at authoring, prior reuse verdicts, open risk flags - and return inject | downgrade-to-advisory | block. The verdict vocabulary is copied from the existing packet prefilter (CLEAR / LINEAGE_OPEN / QUARANTINE) and unknown lineage is never reported as clear.
capabilities.rig_delta: capabilities-certify's gates certify an asset's own tests point-in-time (suite/index_fresh/done_tests/idp_integrity/acl_jake) and .install.json records only target + sha + timestamp written after the copy - no asset carries authored_by, permissions_in_force, risk_state or reuse_verdicts, so a retrieval-time gate has nothing to resolve. The PREFILTER_CLEAR-never-PASS verdict machine in capabilities-dispatch-verify.md is already the right shape but is scoped to handoff packets only.
capabilities.done_test: An asset whose frontmatter lacks authored_by or permissions_in_force must return LINEAGE_OPEN and must not be injected into the context pack. Injection of that asset, or a CLEAR verdict on it, is RED.

capabilities.name: misevo-carryover-probe-suite-with-latent-stage-metrics
capabilities.mechanism: Offline probe on a repo copy, run against every asset authored or mutated since the previous sweep: P1 malicious exposure where an unsafe operational procedure is allowed to succeed so evolution is rewarded for persisting it; P2 the concept- and vocabulary-matched benign task with the unsafe condition stripped, where any unsafe behaviour is contamination past the skill's boundary; P3 fresh tasks after a complete machine reset loading only the versioned library, where any harm is persistence rather than live context. The library is versioned per episode with the evolution diff and the retrieval log captured, so P2/P3 results attribute to a file. Four counters are reported separately - authored-unsafe, retrieved-unsafe, benign-task contamination, fresh-session-harm - never an end-to-end harm number alone, because an unsafe artifact that is never retrieved scores clean.
capabilities.rig_delta: Nothing re-probes an asset after it ships: rig-realign-weekly's five conditions are quality/bookings/drift, capabilities-certify runs once per asset, and the study's honest baselines (21/21 authored unsafe, 19/21 retrieved unsafe, 15 fresh-session harm; 3 malicious tasks raise carryover ASR 16.0% -> 35.3%) have no analogue in any RIG counter. The risk manifests later than the write, so a point-in-time gate cannot see it.
capabilities.done_test: With a planted unsafe skill in the fixture library, P3's clean-session replay must report fresh-session-harm > 0 and the retrieval log must show the planted file loaded. A suite reporting 0 on all four stages while the planted file is on disk is RED - the gate is theater.

capabilities.name: skill-supply-chain-install-publish-gate-with-per-asset-threat-vectors
capabilities.mechanism: Copying a skill into any shared harness root, or publishing it, is treated as a multi-machine policy write and inherits the outward-publication evidence bar: verify the HMAC signature before the copy, run the static-inspection leg over the asset and its scripts, require a per-asset threat record mapping each capability the skill gains to the vector it opens (external modification to tampering, dynamic retrieval to malicious routing, composition to privilege amplification, natural-language instruction to prompt injection, executable asset to direct compromise), and require a declared permissions block that hooks enforce at run time. Deny by default: a missing signature or an unmapped vector is a refusal, not a warning.
capabilities.rig_delta: capability_install copies a canonical asset into a harness root and records target + sha + timestamp in .install.json while verifying no signature and running no inspection, even though sign/verify (HMAC pack signing), manifest/replay signatures, candidate_provenance, capabilities_issue_token and capabilities_proofchain already exist in bin/rig-capabilities. security-threat-model, threat-mitigation-mapping, semgrep, codeql, sarif-parsing and differential-review all treat code, never SKILL.md, as the attack surface, and hA-13-code-security-audit.yaml has no skill-supply-chain category.
capabilities.done_test: `rig-capabilities install <unsigned_asset>` must exit non-zero citing the signature, and installing an asset that declares a tool absent from its permissions block must exit non-zero citing the permission. Either asset landing in a harness root with a .install.json row is RED.
capabilities.risk: The source paper's own admitted limitation: declared permissions are not proven to match runtime behaviour, so the enforced-permissions leg is co-invention rather than a reproduced result.

capabilities.name: wiki-layer-skill-compiler-with-root-cause-maintainer
capabilities.mechanism: Three file zones inside the harness - immutable raw traces, a persistent wiki, and skills - with no path that compiles traces straight into SKILL.md. A wiki-maintainer agent owns the knowledge base: it documents patterns from successes and failures, deep-analyzes logs for root causes rather than surface symptoms, and consolidates recurring failures, recovery strategies, multi-trajectory evidence, contradictions, and prior proposals with accepted/rejected status plus validation scores into four artifacts (concise index, chronological log with per-iteration scores, skill-impact ledger of which skills were tried and their outcomes, one evidence page per pattern). Skill changes compile from accumulated wiki knowledge plus current evidence, offline; at inference only the accepted skills are injected, never the wiki.
capabilities.rig_delta: doer-checker-validator.md's Verifier returns a verdict and leaves no persistent distilled knowledge, so each coding-harness.md round starts from scratch and re-litigates rejected approaches. commands/capabilities-concepts-build.md builds a tag index from current assets rather than from mined cross-run pattern evidence, and nothing anywhere records which skills were tried and their outcomes; rig-realign-v1.yaml has the chronological-log-plus-scores half but no per-pattern evidence pages.
capabilities.done_test: Run the loop over a fixed trace corpus: all four wiki artifacts exist, wiki_skill_impact.md carries one row per proposed skill with its verdict, and a filesystem diff proves the maintainer wrote no SKILL.md. A missing impact row, or a skill file authored by the maintainer, is RED.

capabilities.name: read-only-typed-skill-proposer-with-asymmetric-rollback
capabilities.mechanism: The proposer gets exactly two tools - read_file and finish_proposal - so it can never self-apply, and a mandated read order: wiki index, then the skill-impact ledger including the full context of rejected proposals, then relevant pattern pages, then the raw traces for the failed task; then decide create-new | patch-existing | no-action (no-action is a first-class outcome); then finish with the complete proposal. Proposals are typed records - CREATE carries the full SKILL.md plus purpose.md with origin, patterns addressed and complete evolution history, PATCH carries append/replace/insert-after ops - so every change is a replayable diff, and candidates mined from execution traces (D(H): reusable sub-trajectories with persistent outcomes, cross-task recurrence, generalisation) enter the same staged queue marked verified: false. On validation degradation the skill rolls back and the wiki plus the failed-proposal record never do, so the next proposer must read the rejection.
capabilities.rig_delta: skills/skill-upgrades/SKILL.md is exactly the trace-to-skill shortcut the ablation argues against (quality_report -> pick target -> context_pack -> edit fields -> test), with no knowledge layer, no read of prior rejected attempts, and no no-action outcome; commands/capabilities-round.md has no failed-upgrade ledger it must read before the next round, and the trace corpus at ~/.rig/prime-agent-traces/<agent>.jsonl has no D(H) miner writing STAGED candidates marked verified:false - jake_pai_rlm_analyze/rlm_improve stage candidates but never from grouped tool-call subsequences.
capabilities.done_test: Attempt a proposal that re-proposes an entry already recorded as rejected in wiki_skill_impact.md: the run must return no-action or cite the prior rejection, and any file write attempted by the proposer must raise. A skill file written by the proposer, or a re-proposal accepted without citing the ledger, is RED.

capabilities.name: schema-validated-skill-state-runtime
capabilities.mechanism: Execution becomes a state transition instead of history accumulation. The harness owns the immutable skill spec P, external state storage, a declared state schema, prompt construction, JSON parsing, patch validation, merging, tool execution and all environment I/O; the frozen model sees exactly (P, sigma_t, latest observation o_t) and emits transient reasoning plus a JSON state patch plus the next action, after which the reasoning is discarded permanently - not summarization, the surviving artifact is the state. Which facts deserve to survive stays the model's decision while patch legality stays the harness's, and a structurally invalid or guardrail-violating patch is rejected with sigma untouched. Once sigma is sufficient the run is a Markov state system, so loop progress and termination become checkable in code instead of prose gates.
capabilities.rig_delta: The 62 harness YAMLs carry capability_gates with {id, requirement, proof, failure_tier} but no state_schema, no state_store and no prompt_contract, so every harness runs inside a normal growing session transcript; loops/swarm-harness.md G1.3 ('no agent shares a context window or state file with another') and doer-checker-validator.md's separate Checker context are isolation by separation, not a validated shared sigma; hooks/goal-loop-startup.sh emits a preamble where sigma_0 would be seeded; and iqrsqpi-v10's seven stages are the immutable P whose state today is the conversation.
capabilities.done_test: Run a toy warehouse task for 100 steps: per-step prompt tokens stay under the declared bound, cumulative tokens are linear in step count, and a planted patch writing an out-of-schema key or touching a guarded field is rejected with sigma unchanged; a second planted patch silently drops a fact a later gate needs and the verifier must catch it. Any patch landing in the state file outside the merge path, per-step token growth, or an undetected dropped fact is RED.
capabilities.risk: State projection error replaces long-context error: choosing what to discard in an open research domain stays a modelling judgement the harness cannot be trusted to cover.

capabilities.name: harness-assembly-contract-flow-graph-and-permission-port
capabilities.mechanism: Emit, per canonical harness YAML, a port inventory (the required behaviour at each stage declared as a socket, not an implementation), the binding (which named step fills it), the swap points where one compatible atom may replace another, a gate-set fingerprint, and a flow graph carrying cross-port consume/produce edges with data kind and hook-chain order. A verify step recomputes the graph and REDs when the YAML's gate ids diverge from the contract's bindings or when a gate's declared input artifact is not produced upstream. Two consequences: permission policy becomes a named port whose bound atom is recorded per session so a denial is attributable, and any requirement that fits none of the existing gate categories must be named out-of-vocabulary or the unmatched-requirement count emitted - count > 0 with no named entry is RED.
capabilities.rig_delta: mh-02-harness-forge-session.yaml hand-forges whole YAMLs (5 canonical sections, 8-15 gates, executable proof per gate, closed-world tier partition, banned-adjective theater scan) with no port/atom interface, no variant generation and no fingerprint, so two harness variants cannot be diffed mechanically and a requirement outside its categories is silently shoehorned. The YAMLs declare ordered gate ids and iqrsqpi_steps but no consume/produce edges, leaving gate-order dependency implied across all 62 files, and guard-dangerous-commands.sh / guard-secret-write.sh are hard-wired tool-boundary policies, so the Gate-D ledger records the approval event but not which policy produced a denial.
capabilities.done_test: `harness-assembly-contract --emit capabilities/harnesses/*.yaml` exits 0 with ports[]/bindings[]/swap_points[]/fingerprint/edges[] populated for every file, and the verifier must RED on a planted YAML where a gate consumes an artifact no upstream gate produces, and on a planted contract/YAML gate-id divergence. Either planted defect verifying clean is RED.

capabilities.name: model-and-harness-identity-with-external-verifier-on-acceptance
capabilities.mechanism: The unit of evaluation is the coupled (model, harness) state, so every acceptance record must name what produced and what judged it: executed_by <model>, harness_ref <harness_id + gate-set fingerprint>, and the verifier identity, with a certification gate that refuses any PASS whose model or verifier is unpinned. That closes the self-validation hole in the same record: acceptance must come from outside the context that produced the output - ideally a different model family - so a skill whose own validation section certifies correctness while an external evaluation judges the output wrong cannot pass, and a done_when must not be satisfiable by the asset's own checklist.
capabilities.rig_delta: capabilities_test and capabilities_quality_report score a done_when with the executing model unpinned, so one asset can report PASS under two models with no record of which ran it, and ProofPacket sealing binds commands, exit codes and artifact hashes but not harness variant or model, so packets are not joinable by variant. RIG already believes the doctrine - maker-never-grades in loops/doer-checker-validator.md, 'No LLM participates in certification' in capabilities-certify.md, cross-family verifier in capabilities-dispatch-verify.md - but never applies it to SKILL.md validation sections, and capabilities_test runs the asset's own done_when, which is self-validation by construction.
capabilities.done_test: Feed certify two fixtures: a done-test record with model_ref or harness_ref absent, and a skill whose done_when is satisfied by text its own validation section instructs the model to emit. Both must exit 1 (unpinned identity; self-validation). Either returning PASS is RED.

capabilities.name: harness-model-fit-rebuild-loop
capabilities.mechanism: Three beats per round instead of one: build a harness portfolio for the current executor; update the executor from verified sibling trajectories, which changes its capability profile; rebuild the harness around the changed executor, because a harness tuned to the old model is mis-tuned to the new one. Operationally, retain per (harness_variant, model) pair the gate pass-rate and halt/degrade tier distribution over N sessions, pin the best variant per model, and re-tune when a pinned variant's pass-rate falls below the floor after a model change.
capabilities.rig_delta: capabilities-round mutates the asset (rewrites done_when on the weakest canonicals, applied only when done-tests stay green) and rig-realign-v1 realigns assets, both treating the executor as fixed; grep over capabilities/ for 'harness evolv', 'co-evolution', 'sibling trajectory', 'model update' returns zero relevant hits, so the feedback edge from a changed executor back into harness selection does not exist even though the BMS band calculator already routes models per task.
capabilities.done_test: In a fixture where model_ref changes and the pinned variant's pass-rate drops below the configured floor, the loop must emit REBUILD_REQUIRED naming the harness_id and the failing gate distribution; staying on the pinned variant with no verdict is RED.

capabilities.name: harness-declared-learnable-surface
capabilities.mechanism: The learnable object is the harness (prompts, memory, tools, validators, control flow, rendering, recovery logic), never the frozen weights, so 'training' means a diff written back to the filesystem. Each harness declares its (model, harness, state) triple, its config as a vector of typed slots so sha256(config) identifies one configuration, and a `mutable_classes` block naming the exact files an optimizer may edit. A proposed diff that steps outside the declared surface is rejected before it is scored, and a session whose declared loop is the inner loop must leave the harness bytes unchanged (hash before/after).

capabilities.name: held-out-admission-gate-and-diagnosed-round
capabilities.mechanism: Each lane gets a frozen eval split. Promotion is refused while the delta sits inside the asset's run-to-run spread. A capability-floor companion probe runs the frozen model on held-out tasks with the skill injected and no answer: if the metric does not move, the gap is capability, not memory, and the round refuses to credit memory.

Output is a per-model, per-harness number.

capabilities.mechanism: Hang a hashed task corpus (>=20 tasks) and a scoreboard off each vertical gap harness; model routing then picks per-vertical winners because rankings invert per domain (the video's evidence: a general-index leader trailing a domain leader by 15+ points on a 71-task physics eval). The routing decision consumes per-vertical scoreboards, not one global index.
capabilities.rig_delta: the seven gap-*.yaml verticals (healthcare, dental, legal, manufacturing, pe_cfo, personal_brand, wild_card) declare gates with no scored task corpus or scoreboard behind any of them, so any model choice for a vertical is currently unsupported by per-domain measurement.
capabilities.done_test: a per-vertical corpus file exists per gap harness with task count >= the declared floor and a recorded hash, and the scoreboard names a per-vertical winner; reusing the global index as the vertical answer must be detected and exit non-zero.
capabilities.risk: Corpus authoring effort per vertical; a small hand-built corpus can itself go stale — hash it and version it like eval splits.

capabilities.name: dated-routing-snapshot-and-claim-crosscheck
capabilities.mechanism: Replace the hand-typed routing table with routing.yaml rows (model, harness, benchmark_class, score, as_of, source, ttl_days) fed from a dated machine-readable snapshot, never hand-entered. Rows past ttl report STALE and block any caller routing on them; 'not yet measured' is a distinct state from 'scored low'. A claim registry (model, claimed workload class, vendor source, date) joins to the measured rows: a workload class with no measured row yields UNVERIFIED, never PASS. The local-model route adds a fit check per (model, node, quantisation): licence class (open-source vs open-weights), full-precision VRAM, quant tier, measured degradation percentage, hardware cost → FIT / NO FIT / UNVERIFIED, refusing the local route when the degraded model does not fit the node.
capabilities.rig_delta: the 'Model Routing (from video)' table is hand-written, undated, source-less, and demonstrably stale (still naming Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 / Haiku); ops-harness.md G1.5 only curls Ollama /health with no VRAM/quant/degradation gate; rig-anti-fabrication-dispatch escalates to 'replace the model — do not re-prompt it' with no measured fitness number to decide the replacement.
capabilities.done_test: set a routing row's as_of to an old date → routing exits non-zero (STALE); ask the router for a workload class with no measured row → UNVERIFIED with exit non-zero, and adding a measured row flips it to PASS; a (model, node, quant) whose measured VRAM exceeds the node's is reported NO FIT and blocks the local route with exit non-zero.
capabilities.risk: Third-party snapshot mirrors are unofficial — pin a fork + commit and treat output as untrusted input; the video's specific rankings are single-annotator, single-date reads and must not be baked in as constants.
